title: <An English title named as the side of the company that would issue this paper would name it, on a general subject at the charter's own level of generality, identifying the product by its official display name or tier-family name where that naming would put it; no one title pattern may dominate a product's corpus. Never a question, never an internal-procedure label, never the particular combination of circumstances a task presents, never wording that signals a dependency, a sequence or a remedy, and never words coined for retrieval.>
content:
<English markdown, one topic per document, in the formal register of the paper it purports to be within this company's own knowledge base. The KB and the structured source are in strict bijection at the level of normative semantic atoms: every rule in the source has exactly one bearing document in the prose, and every calculation, eligibility, authorisation, evidence requirement, step, ordering, question, confirmation, wait, review, notification, exception handling and business effect in the prose must trace back to one or more structured source locators. Never add a policy the source does not contain in order to enrich the content, make it feel realistic, or make it safer; in particular, never turn a tool parameter into a 'must ask / must confirm' step, and never add delivery dates, customer confirmations, read-backs, post-action reviews, duplicate guards, corrections, approvals, waits or handoff steps. When the source material is thin, a short document or an omitted section with no source is allowed; there is no minimum word count or average length.

A dependency between problems is stated exactly as the source states it, and no further. For a prerequisite, the blocked policy's hub or one of its fragments carries that edge's prerequisite sentence (the source's `policy_source`) word for word as a formal clause — a sentence that says outright, with an ordering connective, what this policy's result waits on: a record-visible state (the state form) or, as a declared fallback, the depended-on action in business words (the action form) — and may restate it equivalently within the same document, keeping its connective, its strength and its form: a restatement of a state-form sentence never names the action, a performer or the other problem, and no restatement of either form names a tool, a policy or another document. The depended-on policy's own documents state its own rule — what its write books — using the plain business terms the records show, and never say who waits on it. Nothing routes the hop: no tool name, no 'call X first', no ordered steps or sequence of tool names across problems, no dependency table or checklist, no contrast between a wrong and a correct reading, no named mistake. Which write brings a waited-on state about, how the hops chain and in what order the writes land are what the reader works out from the depended-on documents and the records. The source's `condition`, `resolved_by` and `fallback_reason` appear nowhere. Wording elsewhere is free: a rule sentence may be quoted or paraphrased, but never at the cost of a boundary, a base, a strength or a scope. Identifiers the solver must reproduce exactly (tool names, their parameter names and enum values, fixed phrases a tool accepts, the product's official display name) stay exact, in backticks when inside prose.

Form follows the document's origin — the kind of policy-bearing paper it is within this company's own document ecology, assigned in the render plan (skill Value 1), never a list in this template: it sections, numbers, tabulates, runs as continuous clauses or answers questions as that paper would, always formal, every policy-bearing sentence a declarative rule and never an instruction, a step or a route, a section existing only where the source has semantics for it; the rule's shape decides what must be demonstrated, the origin how it looks; no one skeleton, title pattern or opening pattern dominates a product's corpus; and an origin adds no date, reference, version, author or claim the source does not carry. Express every calculation relationship in words (multiplied by / less / total / the higher of), and never use arithmetic symbols, but never compress the base the source rule pins down, its ordering/grouping, its cap/floor, or the point at which it rounds; state a calculation as a definition of the resulting quantity, precise enough that only one reading is natural, never as a procedure or a warning against a wrong reading. The document must make plain early on which product category it governs (naming it verbatim with the official display_name from the charter) and its general subject, opening as its origin would — with the rule, the situation, the figure or the question — never with a scenario, never with a sentence about the document itself, and never with an opening shared with other documents. There must be no table names, field names, event types, parameter keys, policy ids, DSL, row ids, or implementation-facing phrasing such as 'writes to / lands in the table / field'; the only code-shaped tokens allowed are tool names, and, in the parameter section of that tool's own invocation document, that tool's parameter names and enum values. Take one of the following shapes according to role:

[facet document (role=facet)] One facet that genuinely exists in the source, across all tiers: render only the applicable basis from the source and a parameter table covering every tier. The quantitative keys this document carries are declared in meta.carries. Write the exceptions or handling sections only where the source actually has them.

[policy document (role=policy)] The complete equivalent text of one base policy: the rule and all of its eligibility conditions, including the applicable events, the authority boundary between system records and customer statements, and the correlation to the business object of this transaction. Where the source has a time gate, keep the business event the clock starts from, the verifiable record, the day/month counting algorithm for anchor plus duration, the direction of comparison, the equality boundary, and the source's prescribed handling when it is not met; never add negative space, communication actions or exception flows the source does not have. Where an extended policy's overwrite has retired one of this policy's clauses, the clause is still carried here, registered in meta.superseded_clauses and marked in the prose with the controlled wording 'no longer in force'.

[hub document (role=hub)] State the entry point to the policy only as far as the trigger, subject, rule and target tool of that extended policy support, with the applicable situation stated generally; factor names, counts, component inventories, calculation steps, cross-category hints, fragment navigation and reading-completion cues are all forbidden. It states nothing about another problem except, where it is the home of a prerequisite's prerequisite sentence, that sentence verbatim and its same-form equivalents, never another problem's tool name or a route. Do not add reassuring steps such as confirmation, dates, read-backs or reviews. meta must not contain factors/covers, and carries must be empty. When the tool is exclusive to this policy, the hub doubles as the invocation document and sets meta.tool; describe each parameter only as far as task_tools can prove (meaning, format, enum and return), and never turn the existence of a parameter into a policy precondition. When the tool is shared, do not set meta.tool, and do not list parameters or navigate to the tool document.

[computation document (role=baseline)] Exactly one per extended policy that declares factors. Renders the policy's baseline.rule — the standard method and the default values — complete and coherent on its own: which quantities enter the result and from which records, the default rate, fee, allowance or threshold, the standard rounding, window, base and order, and how the inputs assemble into the result, as one formal clause presented as its origin would present a calculation and worked through to a figure on hypothetical inputs. A reader who finds this document and the product figures it names, and nothing else, can compute a definite number; a tier parameter the standard method reads is named in business words. It is silent about anything that modifies it: no 'unless otherwise provided', no 'adjustments may apply', no 'certain customers qualify', no 'set out elsewhere', no exception list, no pointer, and it never calls itself a baseline, a default or a standard calculation subject to anything. meta.covers is exactly the set of compute bindings that belong to no factor (result included); meta.carries is the policy's own baseline.params keys (those that are its params); the product figures it reads are named, their values living in the facet tables.

[factor, an independent policy fragment (role=factor)] Renders exactly one declared factor of the source extended policy (factors[].id): a trigger condition (a ladder of tiers, some of them compound conditions) plus an effect. It carries the whole ladder — every tier's condition in the words the records use, every part of a compound condition, and what that tier does: the value it selects for a parameter factor, or, for a method factor, the computation rule it applies in words (the operation, the base, the rounding mode, precision and moment, the window or day-count convention, the order of steps, the cap moment, the multiplier) — as one formal clause expanded in the forms its origin and the rule's shape call for, every threshold shown on both of its sides and every compound condition in its combinations, in whatever form that origin would give them; no tier is dropped, merged or softened, and the thresholds, windows and values are exact and stated in figures in this document — a must, even where another document of the policy also states the same figure or a business name for the band is defined elsewhere; a ladder that names a band without its figure is incomplete. Where the tier rests on another product's holdings or entries, the prose names that product by its official display name and the kinds of records it reads, without restating that product's rules. The prose never calls itself a factor / satellite / the Nth item, never mentions the hub, the other fragments, the total fragment count or a reading order, never says which tier a customer or most customers fall on, and never describes the reading someone without the rule would take. meta.factor is the source factor id; meta.covers contains every compute binding of that factor. Handling hints and exceptions with no source are not written.

[tool document (role=tool)] For a non-calculating tool, or a calculating tool shared by at least two extended policies. All four sections come only from task_tools.py: the situation of use and the business effect the function can prove, described at the level of the capability rather than the circumstances of a task; how it is invoked and its owner: the tool name verbatim, the word `unlock`, and for a customer-owned tool that the customer themselves runs it after the agent hands it over; the parameter names, the meanings the source can prove, the formats and the full enum sets; and the successful return and explicit errors the source can prove. The existence of a parameter creates no asking or confirmation step; where the source defines no error, review, correction or duplicate-guard behaviour, none may be added.

No document states when to hand off to a human without a structured source for it. Length is determined by how much real information the single source can carry; usually no more than about 2600 characters, though it may exceed that where precisely covering the source genuinely requires it. Padding the length with tables of contents, repeated definitions, navigation, confirmation/review or invented exception flows is forbidden.>

meta.source: <relative path of the source yaml, e.g. env/<scenario>/tasks/<difficulty>/<product>.extended.yaml or env/<scenario>/blueprint/products/<product>.yaml>
meta.role: <hub | baseline | factor | facet | policy | tool — baseline is the computation document of an extended policy (exactly one per policy)>
meta.policy_id: <when role is one of {hub,baseline,factor}: the id of the extended policy it belongs to; when role=policy: the base policy id; omitted otherwise>
meta.tool: <when role is one of {hub,tool}: the name of the task tool for which this document is the invocation document; omitted otherwise>
meta.factor: <when role=factor: the id of the source extended policy's declared factor (factors[].id) this document renders; exactly one document per declared factor, never transcribed into the hub; omitted otherwise>
covers: <required when role is one of {baseline,factor}: the names of the source extended policy compute bindings this document implements. A baseline document lists exactly the bindings that belong to no declared factor, result included; a factor document lists every binding of its declared factor (its evidence bindings and its ladder binding). Every binding is claimed by exactly one document across the whole corpus; omitted for other roles; strictly forbidden on a hub.>
superseded_clauses: <when role=policy and some extended policy's overwrite retires a clause of this base policy: each retired clause quoted verbatim from the base rule; every registered clause is marked 'no longer in force' in content; omitted otherwise>
carries: <the quantitative basis keys this document carries. A hub must be empty; a computation document carries the baseline.params keys that are its own params, a factor its ladder's thresholds and tier values, a facet its tier table's keys — there is no cap on how many; ideally each key appears once across the corpus, a policy's own constants in that policy's documents; a factor document always lists and states in figures the thresholds its own ladder turns on, even if another document also states them (the gate checks only that each key is rendered).>
